title: VPN Service Edges, Network Connectors and BGP Peers dashboards

prose.text: {{ranges}} {{aggregation}} The App Connector, Private Service Edge and Private Cloud Controller dashboards are in [[zpa.troubleshooting.component-dashboards]].

prose.label: BGP Peers dashboard.
prose.text: {{bgp-service}} {{bgp-sessions}} The page's descriptions of the Connect and Active states are its own wording {{gap:bgp-state-wording}}.
BGP configuration is in [[zpa.vpn.bgp]], the components in [[zpa.vpn.service-edges]] and [[zpa.vpn.network-connectors]], and the hub is [[zpa.vpn]].

checks.do: Whether a Peak widget on the Network Connectors dashboard is being read as an average, since Minimum Available Disk Space is not the average over the time frame.
Whether a dashed line on the Network Connectors dashboard is being read as actual data.
Whether two time filters are being compared for the same point in time on the VPN Service Edges or Network Connectors dashboard.

ranges.statement: The VPN Service Edges, Network Connectors and BGP Peers dashboards each show data over a period from 1 hour to 14 days, or a custom range whose start and end dates must be within the last 14 days, and each displays by default information about events that occurred in the last hour.

quotes: View VPN Service Edge data over a period between 1 hour to 14 days, or you can select Custom. If you use a custom range, the start and end dates must be within the last 14 days.
By default, the dashboard displays information about events that occurred in the last hour.
View Network Connector data over a period between 1 hour to 14 days, or you can select Custom Range. If you use a custom range, the start and end dates must be within the last 14 days.
By default, the dashboard displays information about events that occurred in the last hour.
View BGP peers data over a period between 1 hour to 14 days, or you can select Custom Range. If you use a custom range, the start and end dates must be within the last 14 days.
By default, the dashboard displays information about events that occurred in the last hour.

aggregation.statement: On the VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors dashboards, data is aggregated differently for different time period filters, so the same point in time in an Activity Monitor widget might show slightly different values depending on the selected time.

quotes: Due to how data is aggregated for different time period filters, the same point in time in an Activity Monitor widget might show slightly different values depending on the selected time.
Due to how data is aggregated for different time period filters, the same point in time in an Activity Monitor widget might show slightly different values depending on the selected time.

vse-widgets.statement: The VPN Service Edges dashboard displays interactive timeseries charts for the VPN Service Edge selected from the drop-down menu: the total number of Client Connectors currently connected with the bytes received from and sent to them, the total count of Network Connectors currently connected with the throughput received from and sent to them, and the total number of VPN Service Edges deployed in the organization with the bytes received and sent.

quotes: The dashboard displays a series of interactive timeseries charts.
VPN Service Edge selection: Select the VPN Service Edge that you want to view data for from the drop-down menu.
Total Number of Client Connectors: Displays the total count of individual Zscaler Client Connectors that are currently connected to the VPN Service Edge.
Bytes Received from Client Connectors: Displays the volume of data traffic received from Zscaler Client Connectors to monitor inbound traffic from users.
Bytes Sent to Client Connectors: Displays the volume of data traffic sent to Zscaler Client Connectors to monitor outbound traffic to users.
Displays the total count of Network Connectors currently connected to the VPN Service Edge.
Displays the throughput of data received from Network Connectors, showing traffic from your internal networks.
Displays the throughput of data sent to Network Connectors, showing traffic directed towards your internal networks.
Total Number of VPN Service Edges: Displays the total count of VPN Service Edges deployed within your organization.
Bytes Received from VPN Service Edges: Displays the total volume of inbound data processed by the VPN Service Edges from all sources.
Bytes Sent to VPN Service Edges: Displays the total volume of outbound data sent from the VPN Service Edges to all destinations.

nc-widget-limits.statement: On the Network Connectors dashboard, the Top Network Connectors widgets need at least 4 widgets selected to display, with no more than 8 available to view at one time, and the Activity Monitor widgets need at least 4 selected, with no more than 6 available at one time.

quotes: The Top Network Connectors widgets provide an overview of the peak or top metrics for the relevant Network Connectors in the selected time range.
At least 4 widgets must be selected for the widgets to display, and no more than 8 widgets are available to view at one time.
The Activity Monitor widgets provide trend information about selected Network Connectors in the selected time range.
At least 4 widgets must be selected for the widgets to display, and no more than 6 widgets are available to view at one time.

nc-top-widgets.statement: Each Top Network Connectors widget displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors in the selected time frame: Minimum Available Disk Space (those with the least disk space available, not the average disk space used over the time frame), Peak CPU Utilization, Peak Memory Utilization, Peak TCP Port Utilization and Peak UDP Port Utilization (both for IPv4), Peak System File Descriptor Utilization, and Peak Network Connector Throughput (in percentage and bandwidth in bytes).

quotes: Minimum Available Disk Space: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors that have the least disk space available in the selected time frame. This is not the average disk space used over the time frame.
Peak CPU Utilization: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors using the most CPU in the selected time frame.
Peak Memory Utilization: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors using the most memory in the selected time frame.
Peak TCP Port Utilization: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors using the most TCP ports for IPv4 in the selected time frame.
Peak UDP Port Utilization: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors using the most UDP ports for IPv4 in the selected time frame.
Peak System File Descriptor Utilization: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors using the most system file descriptors in the selected time frame.
Peak Network Connector Throughput: Displays up to the top 10 Network Connectors' throughput (in percentage) and bandwidth (in bytes) in the selected time frame.

nc-selection.statement: If no Network Connectors are selected, the top Network Connectors from the Minimum Available Disk Space widget are selected by default for the Activity Monitor widgets. The filters between Network Connectors and Network Connector groups use the OR operator, instead of AND, and at most 25 Network Connectors can be selected at one time. A widget can be searched by name, or by value, using >, < or = operators.

quotes: The Activity Monitor widgets provide trend information about selected Network Connectors in the selected time range. If no Network Connectors are selected, the top Network Connectors from the Minimum Available Disk Space widget are selected by default.
The filters between Network Connectors and Network Connector groups use the OR operator, instead of AND, to help compare Network Connectors in Network Connector groups.
There is a limit of 25 Network Connectors you can select at one time.
or use the following search query options with >, <, or = operators:
name: The name of the Network Connector (e.g., name = MyConnector).
value: A numerical value specific to the widget (e.g., value < 40).

nc-lines.statement: Network Connectors dashboard widgets might show solid lines, which represent actual data for the time period, or dashed lines, which indicate the expected trajectory of the data but are not actual data.

quotes: Solid lines represent actual data for the time period. Dashed lines indicate the expected trajectory of the data, but it isn't actual data.

nc-details.statement: The Network Connector Details table gives each Network Connector's Location, the city and country that the Network Connector is connecting from.

quotes: Location: The city and country that the Network Connector is connecting from.

bgp-service.statement: The BGP Peers dashboard filters its table by VPN Service Edge, with the first option applied by default, and shows that VPN Service Edge's Local AS Number and its BGP service status: Active when the BGP service is running, Inactive when it is not running, and Failed when it failed or crashed.

quotes: VPN Service Edges: Filter the information that appears in the table for a specific VPN Service Edge. By default, the first option is applied.
Local AS Number: The autonomous system number (ASN) assigned to the VPN Service Edge.
Active: The BGP service is running.
Inactive: The BGP service is not running.
Failed: The BGP service failed or crashed.

bgp-sessions.statement: The BGP Peers table shows a Peer AS Number (the ASN assigned to the Network Connector), prefixes sent and received and the session uptime in seconds, and a BGP session status of Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm or Established, where Established is the operational state of a successful BGP session in which routes are advertised and learned.

quotes: Peer AS Number: The ASN assigned to the Network Connector.
Idle: The initial state of the BGP before it initiates a connection or listens for a connection request from a neighboring BGP.
Connect: The BGP has successfully connected to a neighboring BGP peer.

Active: The BGP is actively trying to reopen the TCP connection to the peer after an earlier failure. If successful, it moves to the OpenSent status. If the attempt fails, the status moves back to Connect.
OpenSent: Open messages are exchanged between BGP peers.
OpenConfirm: The BGP has received a valid open message and is waiting for a keepalive message from the neighboring BGP.
Established: The BGP session is fully established, and peers can exchange updates about routes. Routes are advertised and learned. This is the operational state of a successful BGP session.
Prefixes Sent: The number of network prefixes sent to BGP peers informing them on how to reach them.
Prefixes Received: The number of network prefixes received by a router.
Session Uptime (Seconds): The duration for which the Network Connector remained active and functional.

bgp-state-wording.title: Whether the BGP Peers page's state descriptions match standard BGP
bgp-state-wording.detail: The page describes Connect as the BGP having successfully connected to a peer and Active as actively trying to reopen the TCP connection; these are the page's own words and were not checked against another captured source.
